Based on the document "Sustainable Direct Recycling of Lithium-Ion Batteries via Solvent Recovery of Electrode Materials" (cssc-2020), we can find the values of δh for each solvent in Table 1:

| δd [MPa]^1/2 | δp [MPa]^1/2 | δh [MPa]^1/2 | Ra [MPa]^1/2 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PVDF | 17.2 | 12.5 | 9.2 | – |
| NMP | 18.4 | 12.3 | 7.2 | 2.3 |
| DMF | 17.4 | 13.7 | 11.3 | 2.4 |
| EG | 17.0 | 11.0 | 26.0 | 16.9 |
| Water | – | – | 42.3 | – |
| Glycerol | – | – | 29.3 | – |
| Diethylene glycol | – | – | 20.7 | – |

We can see that the values of δh for water, glycerol, ethylene glycol, and diethylene glycol are 42.3 MPa^1/2, 29.3 MPa^1/2, 26.0 MPa^1/2, and 20.7 MPa^1/2, respectively.

Ranking these solvents by their hydrogen-bonding strength δh, we get:

1. Water (42.3 MPa^1/2)
2. Glycerol (29.3 MPa^1/2)
3. Ethylene glycol (26.0 MPa^1/2)
4. Diethylene glycol (20.7 MPa^1/2)

So, the ranking is water > glycerol > ethylene glycol > diethylene glycol.
